name: host - DNS Forward/Reverse Lookup and Brute Force
description: DNS lookups using the host command: forward lookups, specific record type queries (MX, TXT, NS), forward brute force, and reverse PTR sweeps.

variations.description: TXT record lookup (SPF, DMARC, verification tokens)
variations.label: TXT records

variations.description: Forward brute force — append prefix list to domain
variations.command: for ip in $(cat <wordlist>); do host $ip.<domain>; done
variations.label: Subdomain loop (wordlist)

variations.description: Forward brute force — filter resolved hosts only
variations.command: for ip in $(cat <wordlist>); do host $ip.<domain>; done | grep -v 'not found'
variations.label: Subdomain loop (filter misses)

variations.description: Reverse sweep — PTR lookups across address range
variations.command: for ip in $(seq <start> <end>); do host <prefix>.$ip; done | grep -v 'not found'
variations.label: Numeric range loop

variations.description: Lookup specific IP via reverse DNS
variations.label: host lookup

examples.label: Forward brute force with wordlist
examples.command: for ip in $(cat list.txt); do host $ip.megacorpone.com; done

examples.label: Forward brute force — show only resolved hosts
examples.command: for ip in $(cat list.txt); do host $ip.megacorpone.com; done | grep -v 'not found'

examples.label: Reverse PTR sweep over /24 range
examples.command: for ip in $(seq 200 254); do host 51.222.169.$ip; done | grep -v 'not found'

notes: host is a simple, clean DNS utility — good for quick record queries and loop-based brute force scripts. For forward brute force: build a wordlist of common hostnames (admin, mail, vpn, dev, test, staging, etc.) and iterate `host $prefix.<domain>`. Filter NXDOMAIN responses with `grep -v 'not found'`. For reverse sweeps: iterate a range of the last octet over the known netblock prefix and filter results. Reverse PTR records often reveal internal naming conventions (srv01, dc01, sql-prod) that expose infrastructure layout. TXT records may expose SPF sources (third-party services), DKIM selectors, or verification tokens revealing cloud providers. Chaining: host for quick forward/reverse lookups → dnsenum for comprehensive automated enumeration → nmap against discovered hosts.

references.title: OffSec PEN-200 - Penetration Testing with Kali Linux

recommended.note: Run WHOIS first to get netblock ranges and nameservers to target.
Follow up with dnsenum for comprehensive automated DNS enumeration including AXFR attempts.
Feed discovered IPs from PTR sweep to nmap for port scanning.

defense.why_it_works: DNS is an open directory by design. PTR records in reverse zones and subdomain brute force against public resolvers require no authentication — if DNS zones are not carefully curated, internal topology is exposed.
defense.prerequisites: DNS resolver reachable. Target domain known. For reverse sweeps: netblock range known (from WHOIS).
defense.misconfiguration: Reverse PTR zone populated with internal server names. Internal hostnames resolvable via public DNS. No DNS firewall/RPZ to block external subdomain brute force queries.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Reverse zone exposing internal naming
$ORIGIN 169.222.51.in-addr.arpa.
200 PTR dc01.corp.megacorpone.com.
201 PTR sql-prod.corp.megacorpone.com.
defense.secure_config:
# Remove PTR records for internal hosts from public-facing reverse zones
# Use split-horizon DNS: internal zone has full records, external zone has only public IPs
defense.impact: Reveals internal hostname conventions, number of servers, server roles (dc, sql, vpn, mail) — accelerates lateral movement planning.
defense.detection: High NXDOMAIN rate from single source (subdomain brute force). Sequential PTR lookups across a /24 range. Both visible in DNS server query logs.
defense.artifacts: DNS query logs, passive DNS databases recording the brute force patterns.
defense.prevention: Split-horizon DNS. Remove PTR records for internal hosts from external reverse zones. Implement DNS firewall / Response Policy Zones to flag or block known brute-force patterns.
defense.evasion: Use slow request rate to stay below NXDOMAIN threshold alerts. Query from multiple source IPs.
